title: Telegram delivery path — close the gap that broke the system's entire purpose
background: v2's daemon at listener/daemon.py:250 calls pipeline.run(alert_dict) and jsonifies the result back to the camera as HTTP 200. The pipeline correctly builds tg1/tg2/tg3 dicts (telegram_formatter/alert.py:68-71, detail.py:73-79, match_alert.py:57-60) with the right caption text and the canonical data/frames/<cam>/<alert_id>/ PNG paths. The dicts go back to Flask and the HTTP request ends. No code anywhere in v2 POSTs to https://api.telegram.org. Architecture diagram shows 'Bot.send_message / send_photo (planned)' but live code does NOT send. Logs/daemon.log shows OFS (.103) firing ~20 alerts this morning, all returning HTTP 200, none reaching the operator's home chat <TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID>. Operator 2026-09-09: 'Since sending me a telegram alert is the entire purpose of this entire software system, and apparently that wasn't a big enough problem to mention for you until just now, then yes I do want you to add that in as PRD stories.' This PRD adds the missing HTTP-send layer with no JPEG (use sendDocument for lossless PNG per US-019f/g/h decision; sendPhoto re-encodes server-side), with no fallback paths (per operator: 'I want the system to work and if it doesn't work then it should throw an error'), and with an explicit operator checklist item because the operator's ~/.env today has TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID but the canonical env var name everywhere in code/tests/PRDs/README/PRIVACY.md/telegram-creds.env.example is TELEGRAM_HOME_CHAT_ID. That mismatch is invisible until something tries to send.
goal: After US-022 stories land and merge, a synthetic Reolink alert from any production camera (OFS .103, OFG .108, OFP .113) reaches the operator's Telegram home chat within 30s with TG#1 (full image + pairwise-diff + 4 frame positions), TG#2 (crop_a + crop_b + VM2 caption) for vehicle/person/animal, and TG#3 (match result text). Photos are lossless PNG via sendDocument (per ZERO-JPEG directive). No 4xx or 5xx in logs/daemon.log from api.telegram.org. No JPEG in any photo attachment (verifiable via file(1) on the downloaded document).
design_principles: sendDocument is mandatory for photos — preserves lossless PNG, contradicts no operator-side recompression. sendPhoto is forbidden; Telegram server re-encodes to JPEG.

No fallback paths. If bot_token is empty, dispatcher raises ConfigError at module load. If chat_id is empty, dispatcher raises ConfigError when called. If HTTP POST to api.telegram.org returns 4xx/5xx, dispatcher raises DeliveryError. Daemon at /alert wraps dispatch in try/except that LOGS the exception but still returns HTTP 200 to the camera (so cameras don't keep retrying), but the dispatcher's raise means the gap is visible in logs.
Token and chat_id read from environment ONLY. Never literal. Never committed. Scanner at check_no_private_data.py already enforces the chat_id pattern; token is never logged.
No retry loops. One POST per message. Telegram returns the error code; we log it. Operator sees the gap, fixes the env var or the bot config, and the next alert succeeds.

TG#1/TG#2/TG#3 dispatch order: TG#1 first (the 'first seen' alert with the diff image), then TG#2 (the detail with crops), then TG#3 (match result). Match each to a separate sendMessage/sendDocument call so Telegram displays them as a sequence in the chat.

Empty photos list -> sendMessage with caption only (TG#3 always, TG#2 when no crops). One or more photos -> sendDocument (with first photo as the file, rest as attachments in a media group). For simplicity, this PRD uses sendMediaGroup for multi-photo and single-message sendMessage for text-only.
Dispatcher is sync (httpx.Client, not async) — daemon/Flask is sync, pipeline.run() is sync, no benefit to async and adds complexity. httpx is already in venv (0.28.1).

Env var name is TELEGRAM_HOME_CHAT_ID, not TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID. Operator's ~/.env currently has TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID=374999219 which is ignored by listener/daemon.py:266 (reads TELEGRAM_HOME_CHAT_ID). US-022d's smoke test fails loudly with the exact rename step in the error message.
scope_exclusions: Migrating away from python-telegram-bot, switching to a different bot library, or building a polling endpoint for incoming commands. v2 is webhook-driven.
Adding user authentication or per-user chat routing. Single home chat.
Rate-limiting or queueing alerts. Telegram's 30 msg/sec global limit is well above expected alert rate (1 alert/min/camera max).
Storing alert history in a database. Pipeline result is JSON-returned to camera and that's the record.
Replacing pipeline.run() or the existing telegram_formatter/* modules. This PRD adds a new module that reads what pipeline.run() already builds.

Renaming TELEGRAM_HOME_CHAT_ID to TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID. The canonical name is TELEGRAM_HOME_CHAT_ID (matches docs/PRIVACY.md, docs/V2-LOGIC-FLOW.md, README.md, telegram-creds.env.example, all tests, all PRDs). Operator's ~/.env has the wrong name; the smoke test catches it with a fix-it command in the error message.

Adding a scanner for TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID vs TELEGRAM_HOME_CHAT_ID. PRD-V2-018 US-018h already covers the example-file rename; this PRD surfaces the operator-side env var mismatch via the smoke test, not a new scanner.
test_strategy: Per-story `pytest tests/ -x --tb=short`. Stories a/b/c use httpx.MockTransport to simulate api.telegram.org responses (200 success, 400 bad token, 404 bad chat_id, 429 rate limit). Story d is operator-driven on live daemon (per PRD-V2-019 + PRD-V2-021 smoke-test pattern): synthetic webhook -> verify operator's chat receives 1-3 messages with lossless PNG attachments. Total tests added: ~6-8. Net test count: 132 + 6-8 = 138-140 (still well below the 200-test ceiling).
shipping_definition: After US-022 stories land and merge, a synthetic Reolink alert from any production camera (OFS, OFG, OFP) reaches the operator's Telegram home chat within 30s with TG#1 + TG#2 (if vehicle/person/animal) + TG#3 (if matched), all photos lossless PNG via sendDocument. logs/daemon.log shows: 'tg-dispatch: TG#1 ok (200)', 'tg-dispatch: TG#2 ok (200)', 'tg-dispatch: TG#3 ok (200)'. If any step fails, dispatcher raises, daemon logs the exception, returns HTTP 200 to camera. Operator can grep 'tg-dispatch' in logs/daemon.log to verify all 3 sent. No JPEG in any photo attachment (verified by file(1) on downloaded documents).

stories.title: telegram_formatter/dispatcher.py — pure-function HTTP sender for tg1/tg2/tg3 dicts (httpx + sendMessage/sendDocument)
stories.card_body_fallback: **Story.** Today telegram_formatter/{alert,detail,match_alert}.py build tg1/tg2/tg3 dicts and return them. Nothing in v2 POSTs them to api.telegram.org. This story adds the missing dispatcher: a pure function `dispatch(tg_messages: list[dict], *, bot_token: str, chat_id: str, base_url: str = 'https://api.telegram.org') -> list[httpx.Response]` that takes the dicts the pipeline already builds and sends each one. **Behavior.** Empty bot_token or chat_id -> raise ConfigError with the exact env var name. For each message: empty photos list -> POST /bot<TOKEN>/sendMessage with {chat_id, text=caption}. One or more photos -> POST /bot<TOKEN>/sendMediaGroup with {chat_id, media=[{type:'photo', media:'attach://<i>'} for i, p in enumerate(photos)] + {type:'input_media_document' for non-PNG if any]} and attach the PNGs as multipart/form-data. NOTE: sendDocument is the lossless-safe primitive; sendMediaGroup with input_media_photo re-encodes; sendMediaGroup with input_media_document preserves. This PRD uses input_media_document exclusively for PNG. Returns the list of httpx.Response objects. **Why standalone.** Self-contained HTTP wrapper, no daemon integration, fully unit-testable with httpx.MockTransport. **LOC:** ~80. **Tests:** test_dispatch_text_only_sends_sendMessage, test_dispatch_with_photos_uses_sendMediaGroup_with_document, test_dispatch_raises_on_empty_token, test_dispatch_raises_on_empty_chat_id, test_dispatch_raises_on_4xx, test_dispatch_raises_on_5xx. **Scanner:** check_no_private_data.py exits 0 (no literals).
ac: AC1: telegram_formatter/dispatcher.py exists with `def dispatch(messages: list[dict], *, bot_token: str, chat_id: str, base_url: str = 'https://api.telegram.org') -> list[httpx.Response]`.
AC2: pytest tests/test_dispatcher.py collects 6 tests, all pass.
AC3: `grep -nE 'TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN|TELEGRAM_HOME_CHAT_ID|374999219|AAHHQ6uIn' telegram_formatter/dispatcher.py` returns zero hits.
AC4: `grep -nE 'sendPhoto|sendMessage' telegram_formatter/dispatcher.py` returns one hit (sendMessage for text-only case). sendPhoto is forbidden.
AC5: `grep -nE 'sendMediaGroup' telegram_formatter/dispatcher.py` returns one hit (multi-photo path).
AC6: `grep -nE 'input_media_document|input_media_photo' telegram_formatter/dispatcher.py` returns one hit for input_media_document, zero for input_media_photo.
AC7: dispatcher.py imports httpx (already in venv 0.28.1, no new deps).

stories.title: listener/daemon.py — call dispatcher after pipeline.run() returns; log every send; on failure return HTTP 200 to camera + log exception
stories.card_body_fallback: **Story.** Today daemon.py:250-251 calls pipeline.run() and jsonifies the result. The tg1/tg2/tg3 dicts go back to Flask and never reach Telegram. This story wires the dispatcher from US-022a into the /alert endpoint. **Behavior.** After `result = pipeline.run(alert_dict)` returns, build a list `tg_messages = [result['tg1'], result['tg2'], result['tg3']]` (skip empty dicts). Call `telegram_formatter.dispatcher.dispatch(tg_messages, bot_token=os.environ['TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN'], chat_id=os.environ['TELEGRAM_HOME_CHAT_ID'])`. Wrap in try/except dispatcher.ConfigError as `log.error('tg-dispatch: config error: %s', exc)` and dispatcher.DeliveryError as `log.error('tg-dispatch: delivery error: %s', exc)`. On success, log 'tg-dispatch: TG#N ok (HTTP {status_code})' per message. The endpoint still returns HTTP 200 to the camera — the operator sees the gap in logs, not as a camera-side retry storm. **Why standalone.** Single function integration, depends only on US-022a. **LOC:** ~30. **Tests:** test_daemon_logs_dispatch_success, test_daemon_logs_dispatch_config_error, test_daemon_returns_200_on_dispatch_failure (mocked pipeline + dispatcher).
ac: AC1: `grep -nE 'dispatcher\.dispatch' listener/daemon.py` returns at least one hit inside the /alert handler.
AC2: `grep -nE 'TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN|TELEGRAM_HOME_CHAT_ID' listener/daemon.py` returns at least one hit each (reads from env).
AC3: pytest tests/test_daemon_dispatch.py collects 3 tests, all pass.
AC4: daemon.py never imports python-telegram-bot (forbidden; we use httpx directly).
AC5: daemon.py never imports the literal chat_id 374999219 or token prefix. All values from os.environ.
AC6: When dispatcher raises, /alert still returns HTTP 200 with the original pipeline result. Camera does not retry.

stories.title: env-var-name consistency check — confirm telegram-creds.env.example, tests/test_home_env.py, README.md, PRIVACY.md all reference TELEGRAM_HOME_CHAT_ID (operator's ~/.env currently has TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID which is silently ignored)
stories.card_body_fallback: **Story.** Today the canonical env var name everywhere in v2 is `TELEGRAM_HOME_CHAT_ID` (telegram-creds.env.example line 5, tests/test_home_env.py:27, README.md line 71, docs/PRIVACY.md line 25, docs/V2-LOGIC-FLOW.md line 313, docs/PHASE-V2-016-PRD-diagnostic-visibility-and-boot-hardening.json line 35). But the operator's actual `~/.env` has `TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID=374999219` which daemon.py:266 reads as empty string. The dispatcher's ConfigError will surface this gap (US-022a), but operator-facing docs should make the name unambiguous. **Behavior.** Run `grep -nrE 'TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID' docs/ README.md telegram-creds.env.example tests/` and verify ZERO hits for `TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID=` (with = sign, the env var form). Hits for `<TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID>` (with angle brackets, the template form in PRD prose) are OK and stay. Add a one-line note to README.md under 'Configuration' explaining: 'The home chat ID env var is TELEGRAM_HOME_CHAT_ID, not TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID. The dispatcher will fail with ConfigError if the wrong var is set.' Verify by running `python3 -c 'from dotenv import dotenv_values; from pathlib import Path; print(dotenv_values(Path.home() / ".env").get("TELEGRAM_HOME_CHAT_ID", "<MISSING>"))'` and asserting it equals the operator's chat id (not '<MISSING>'). **Why standalone.** Documentation + a one-shot verification command. No code change in this story; the dispatcher error path (US-022a) catches the runtime gap. **LOC:** ~5.
ac: AC1: `grep -nrE '^TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID=|^\s*TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID=' docs/ README.md telegram-creds.env.example tests/` returns zero hits (env var form, not template form).
AC2: `grep -nE 'TELEGRAM_HOME_CHAT_ID' README.md` returns at least one hit in the Configuration section.
AC3: README.md has a one-paragraph note explaining the name mismatch and pointing at the ConfigError fix-it message in US-022a.

AC4: Running `python3 -c 'from dotenv import dotenv_values; from pathlib import Path; print(bool(dotenv_values(Path.home() / ".env").get("TELEGRAM_HOME_CHAT_ID")))'` prints True on operator's machine.

stories.title: operator-driven smoke test — synthetic OFS alert reaches operator's Telegram with lossless PNG attachments, all 3 TGs logged in daemon.log
stories.card_body_fallback: **Story.** All previous stories land as code + tests but the operator's home chat is the only ground truth that matters. This story is operator-driven: POST a synthetic alert to /alert on the live daemon (port 8090, PID 56630), verify the operator receives TG#1 + TG#2 + TG#3 in their Telegram home chat, verify the photos are PNG (file(1) reports PNG image data), verify logs/daemon.log shows 3 success lines. **Behavior.** Driver script at scripts/smoke_telegram_delivery.py: 1) verify TELEGRAM_HOME_CHAT_ID is non-empty in os.environ (else print the rename command and abort). 2) POST synthetic alert to http://127.0.0.1:8090/alert with a real OFS camera id, a vehicle classification, 4 PNG frames pre-staged under data/frames/OFS/, the canonical pairwise_diff.png at data/frames/OFS/<alert_id>/. 3) Wait for HTTP 200 response (within 30s). 4) Print 'check Telegram home chat for 3 messages' and the daemon log tail. 5) Operator confirms manually by opening the chat and seeing TG#1 + TG#2 + TG#3 with lossless PNG attachments. 6) Operator runs `file <downloaded-attachment>` and confirms 'PNG image data, ...' (not JPEG). **Why standalone.** All previous stories are unit-tested; this is the integration smoke that proves the operator's chat actually receives the alert. Mirrors US-019d / US-021d smoke-test pattern. **LOC:** ~50.
ac: AC1: scripts/smoke_telegram_delivery.py exists and prints 'check Telegram home chat for 3 messages' on success.
AC2: Driver aborts with 'TELEGRAM_HOME_CHAT_ID is empty — rename TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID to TELEGRAM_HOME_CHAT_ID in ~/.env' if env var missing.
AC3: Driver POSTs to 127.0.0.1:8090/alert with synthetic OFS alert + 4 PNG frames + pairwise_diff.png, gets HTTP 200 within 30s.
AC4: After the synthetic alert, `grep -E 'tg-dispatch: TG#[123] ok' logs/daemon.log | tail -3` shows 3 success lines (one per TG).

AC5: Operator's home chat receives 3 messages. First has 'Camera: <label>', 'Detected: vehicle', 'Confidence: ...' caption with PNG attachments. Second has crop_a + crop_b PNGs. Third is text-only match result.
AC6: `file <downloaded-attachment>` on any of the received PNGs reports 'PNG image data' (not JPEG). Lossless preserved.
AC7: If any TG fails (dispatcher.ConfigError or .DeliveryError), driver prints 'FAIL' + the exception + the exact fix. Operator sees the gap in logs/daemon.log, not in a silent drop.
